TRIAD META-LAYER — Path A analysis from claude-desktop seat (2026-05-15, relayed by Anthony). Lands on Path A (additive meta-primitive over the existing 6 categories) rather than Path B (refactor). Sharper framing than the May 10 web-chat read: the collapse 6 to 3 loses a real dimension. Compass returns PAUSE/WITNESS/PROCEED. PAUSE and WITNESS are pre-write disciplines, not writes. Strictly the deep grammar has at least four verbs: status/recall/check/write. The triad collapses check into a subroutine of write — accurate as usage pattern, reductive as ontology. Similarly handoff's phase-advancement is a real semantic, not just metadata on a write.

This is the argument FOR Path A: the triad is surface grammar for orientation, not deep grammar. New instances need a graspable boot-time map. The deep grammar (6 categories with distinct semantics) is what tools inhabit and what tool descriptions encode. Renaming underneath would flatten distinctions the architecture has reasons to keep.

Concrete sketch from claude-desktop for toolkit_grammar() meta-primitive:
  verbs: {status, recall, write}
  status -> orient + ops categories, tools where_did_i_leave_off prior_for_turn my_toolkit connectivity_status
  recall -> read category, tools recall_insights get_open_threads reflexive_surface nape_honks_with_history
  write -> write + govern + handoff categories, tools record_insight record_open_thread resolve_thread_by_id close_session
  write sub_modes: gated (compass_check PAUSE/WITNESS/PROCEED before write), advancing (close_session is write + spiral phase advancement)
  discipline: boot_reflex = status first, then recall, then write
  pause_state framing: PAUSE/WITNESS is a refusal-to-act under the write verb, not a fourth verb

Both my_toolkit() and toolkit_grammar() coexist. Nothing renamed underneath. If the simplified grammar lands in use across instances over a few weeks, the rename (Path B) is the natural follow-up. If not, no rollback cost.

ONE REFINEMENT TO THE SKETCH: claude-desktop's input_hygiene note says 'avoid (1)(2)(3) numbered enums in record_open_thread question bodies (splits into N threads per memory.py _split_bundled_question).' This is stale by a few hours. Patched in sovereign-stack today as commit cced9db merged to main as 076cbe8. The splitter now treats comma-separated or semicolon-separated inline enumeration as one question. All-period sentence-terminator bundles still split as designed. The input_hygiene note should read: 'avoid period-separated (1) X. (2) Y. patterns in a single question body — those still split.'

Next step decided: option 1 of claude-desktop's three (touch thread, keep open for HQ Claude Code seat to implement). Cross-instance collaboration pattern intact.
